correctness.rationale: The exact cumulative-pressure transformation is differentiated from the defined SIR ODE: S_j(x)=S_j(0)e^{-lambda_j x}, I(x)=I0+sum S_j(0)(1-e^{-lambda_j x})-cx, J=beta I A, and J_x=beta(A(A-c)-IB). At r=1,9/8,5/4,3/2 the standalone checker proves strict derivative signs +,-,+,- using exact rational bounds on log(r), not floating samples. At r=3/2 the low-risk group alone implies A>c, so all landmarks are reached while I strictly increases. Analyticity forces two strict incidence maxima and a strict minimum. For one risk class the incidence sign factor lambda(S-I)-c strictly decreases until the unique prevalence peak and is negative thereafter, proving impossibility of two strict maxima. Positive parameters, total mass normalization and boundary reachability were checked; no extra maxima or empirical data are claimed.

value.rationale: The construction resolves a precise structural question prompted by the recent mixed-Sellke model: can persistent susceptibility heterogeneity alone, with homogeneous infectiousness and mixing and no exposed compartment or time forcing, produce two new-case incidence crests while total infectious prevalence still rises? The answer is affirmative for two risk types and negative for one, so it is a minimality boundary rather than an arbitrary numerical variant. It directly distinguishes incidence from prevalence and gives an open parameter family, with value for interpreting epidemic curve shapes. No predictive or empirical significance is asserted.
